account: Similipal Tiger Reserve in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, runs a network of TrailGuard AI trail cameras. The cameras classify humans, animals and vehicles and send images to a control room. The New Indian Express reports that camera monitoring in the reserve began in October 2024 with about 50 cameras. In May 2025 Ommcom News reported that TrailGuard photographs helped track three poachers, whom a court sent to judicial custody after it rejected their bail. Late on Wednesday 18 February 2026 the cameras detected a group of armed intruders entering the reserve. Field Director Prakash Chand Gogineni said that the real-time alerts mobilized the Similipal South Division, three ranges and three Special Tiger Protection Force units. After about 24 hours of combing, at least 39 poachers surrendered. Nine guns, gunpowder and more than 20 bows and arrows were recovered. A case was registered at Jenabil Wildlife Range. On 27 February 2026 The New Indian Express reported that the network had grown to more than 220 cameras. The newspaper reported that the cameras had helped the reserve detect more than 110 intrusions and arrest nearly 300 poachers and wildlife criminals, and that the reserve was buying 450 more cameras. Gogineni said that the reserve planned to install cameras in at least half of its 1,375 monitoring grids. Later detections on 11 April, around 24 July and 23 September 2026 led to arrests. Courts refused bail to the July and September groups. The camera count varies by source. The Field Director gave “around 220” in February 2026, and The Hans India gave “over 220” in July 2026. The Times of India reported in April 2026 that 50 AI cameras were in use, up from an initial 10, with 300 planned.

ai_role.statement: The AI cameras' real-time detection of the armed group is the stated trigger for the mobilization. That operation ended in surrender and seizure. The park authority's statement is the Field Director's on-record account, quoted by The New Indian Express and the Times of India. The court remands are reported in the press by PTI, Hans India and Ommcom. The cited account lacks corroboration from an available official press note or court order. The account rests on press-quoted forest-department statements.

fields.account: Similipal Tiger Reserve in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, runs a network of TrailGuard AI trail cameras. The cameras classify humans, animals and vehicles and send images to a control room. The New Indian Express reports that camera monitoring in the reserve began in October 2024 with about 50 cameras. In May 2025 Ommcom News reported that TrailGuard photographs helped track three poachers, whom a court sent to judicial custody after it rejected their bail. Late on Wednesday 18 February 2026 the cameras detected a group of armed intruders entering the reserve. Field Director Prakash Chand Gogineni said that the real-time alerts mobilized the Similipal South Division, three ranges and three Special Tiger Protection Force units. After about 24 hours of combing, at least 39 poachers surrendered. Nine guns, gunpowder and more than 20 bows and arrows were recovered. A case was registered at Jenabil Wildlife Range. On 27 February 2026 The New Indian Express reported that the network had grown to more than 220 cameras. The newspaper reported that the cameras had helped the reserve detect more than 110 intrusions and arrest nearly 300 poachers and wildlife criminals, and that the reserve was buying 450 more cameras. Gogineni said that the reserve planned to install cameras in at least half of its 1,375 monitoring grids. Later detections on 11 April, around 24 July and 23 September 2026 led to arrests. Courts refused bail to the July and September groups. The camera count varies by source. The Field Director gave “around 220” in February 2026, and The Hans India gave “over 220” in July 2026. The Times of India reported in April 2026 that 50 AI cameras were in use, up from an initial 10, with 300 planned.

purpose: Detect human intruders and poachers entering the reserve in near real time so rangers can intercept them before wildlife is killed.

ratings.reason: No source documents an injury to rangers that the operation avoided. The reports describe arrests and seizures.
